title: Signal latch: control plane weekly check-in
content:
Context: quick midweek sync focused on recent quota anomalies, an auth regression surfaced during the canary rollout, and a follow-up on routing fallthrough behavior. This doc captures raw notes, decisions, action items, and open questions for triage.

Attendees (stand-in rota): Aisha (notes), Marco, Renee, Jamal, Priya, Zev (joined for 15m)

Top-line updates
- Quotas: Spike on 2026-06-13 02:10–02:35 UTC where several internal test clients hit sudden 429s. Root cause narrowed to a mis-ordered cache invalidation in the quota service (JIRA-PLTFM-4321).
- Auth: Canary of auth-v3 (short-lived tokens + new introspection cache) showed 0.7% 401 increase in canary region vs baseline. Initial hypothesis: token refresh race for long-lived streaming sessions.
- Routing: Safe-fallback policy exercised during the quota spike; routing did fall through to lower-cost pool as designed but latency p95 increased ~120ms for affected requests. No customer-facing incidents.
- Control plane perf: Minor controller GC pause saw control-plane reconciliation lag by ~700ms during the spike window. SRE to correlate memory allocation metrics.

Notes / observations
- Quotas: Jamal reproduced the invalidation order locally. The sequence was: update persistent store -> publish invalidation -> process invalidation -> send ack. Race occurs if invalidation processed before store commit is visible to other nodes. Short-term mitigation: add a sequence-id guard in worker to ignore invalidations with seq < store-last-applied. Medium-term: make invalidation publication part of the same transaction (follow JIRA-PLTFM-4321).
- Auth: Renee observed the 401s were concentrated on streaming endpoints that use token refresh extension. The introspection cache TTL of 4s seems low; changing to 12s reduced fail rate in canary by ~0.4 percentage points in local repro. But increasing TTL has downstream risk if tokens are revoked quickly. Need to consult security on tradeoffs.
- Routing: The fallthrough route picks fallback-pool-b (gpu-mixed) which has slightly higher latency but is cheaper. The decision to prefer cost over latency is expected in policy v1 for non-SLA customers. For SLA customers we should pin to high-priority pools; check policy config for customer tier mapping — Priya to verify no customers were incorrectly classified.

Decisions made in meeting
- Rollback auth-v3 canary? No. We will pause expansion and deploy a small mitigation (increase introspection-TTL to 8s for canary only and add extra metrics around token-refresh errors). If metrics worsen, we will rollback. Owner: Renee. ETA: 6/16.
- Quota fix staging patch: apply seq-id guard in worker and run chaos tests for 48h. Owner: Jamal. ETA: 6/15 for staging, 6/18 for prod rollout (gradual).
- Routing observability: add a per-request trace tag when a fallback route is used and include pool-id. Owner: Marco. ETA: 6/20.

Action items (concrete)
- Jamal: PR with seq-id guard + unit tests (JIRA-PLTFM-4321). Target: 6/15.
- Renee: Deploy TTL tweak to canary, add alert for streaming 401-rate > 0.5% over baseline in 15m window. Target: 6/16.
- Priya: Audit customer-tier mapping for routing policies and confirm none were mis-labeled during the spike. Post results in this doc. Target: 6/16.
- Marco: Instrument fallback traces and wire into console dashboard (add a small table for fallback counts by pool and time). Target: 6/20.
- Aisha: Summarize postmortem draft for quota spike and circulate to cplane+SRE. Target: 6/18.
- SRE (Zev): Correlate GC pause timeline with control-plane prom metrics and kube events; note any correlation with heavy reconciliation loops. Target: 6/15.

Open questions / risks
- Token revocation semantics: If we extend introspection TTL we could delay detection of revoked tokens — risk to security posture. Need security sign-off and mitigations (short-lived revocation broadcast?).
- Quota invalidation atomicity: how large is the blast radius if a sequence-id guard merely masks the race? Need an end-to-end test that simulates cross-zone commit delays.
- Observable dataset for fallback decisions: current logs show fallback counts but we lack a compact SLO for how often fallbacks happen per customer over a week. Suggest adding a weekly rollup metric.

Volunteer ideas / experiments
- Jamal + Marco: run a chaos test where quota store commit is delayed artificially for 30s for one replica to reproduce real-world race behavior. If reliable, escalate to full transactional pub/sub design.
- Priya: propose a mapping sanity-check job that runs nightly to detect customers with inconsistent tier tags across subsystems (billing vs control plane vs console).

Quick metrics snapshot (baseline vs anomaly window)
- p95 downstream latency baseline: 180ms -> spike window 300ms (affected requests)
- 5xx rate baseline: 0.02% -> spike window 0.05%
- auth 401 rate baseline (streaming): 0.1% -> canary 0.8% (auth-v3 initial deploy)
- fallback usage: 32 fallbacks/min during spike window (normal <3/min)

Hand-off notes (who owns what during weekend)
- Jamal: monitor quota alarms and be primary for paging (pager on for JIRA-PLTFM-4321).
- Renee: own auth canary rollout dashboard and escalation path to security if 401 spike crosses 1%.
- Marco: fallback trace dashboard + brief runbook update: how to force routing pin if needed.

Quick links
- Quota spike replay script: github.com/redwood-inference/platform-tests/quotareplay (branch: spike-2026-06)
- Canary dashboard (short): console.redwood.internal/dashboards/canary-auth-v3

Notes to self (informal)
- Remember to add the 'seq-id' metric to prom so we can graph invalidation sequence gaps over time.
- Ask security if we can short-circuit revocations by pushing a small immediate invalidation on critical tokens.

Next sync: Friday 2026-06-18 10:30 PT — shorter follow-up to review staging runs and canary metrics (15–20m).

End of notes.
